A ball can leave the platform in two ways:
1. It is struck by its own piston – we call this an ejection (you win).
2. It is in the first slot when either of the other two pistons fires – then it simply rolls away (you lose).

Treat the progress of a single ball through the three slots as a Markov chain.
State 3 = ball in third slot, State 2 = second slot, State 1 = first slot.

With each step one of the three pistons fires, each with probability 1⁄3.

Transitions for the chosen ball:
• From 3: 1⁄3 → ejected, 1⁄3 → state 1, 1⁄3 → state 2.
• From 2: 1⁄3 → ejected, 2⁄3 → state 1.
• From 1: 1⁄3 → ejected, 2⁄3 → lost.

Let E₁, E₂, E₃ be the eventual ejection probabilities from states 1,2,3.
E₁ = 1⁄3.
E₂ = 1⁄3 + (2⁄3)E₁ = 1⁄3 + 2⁄9 = 5⁄9.
E₃ = 1⁄3 + (1⁄3)E₁ + (1⁄3)E₂ = 1⁄3 + 1⁄9 + 5⁄27 = 17⁄27.

Now look at the initial setup:
• Ball 1 starts in state 1 → win chance 1⁄3.
• Ball 2 starts in state 2 → win chance 5⁄9.
• Ball 3 starts in state 3 → win chance 17⁄27 ≈ 0.63.
• Every later ball, when it first appears on the platform, also enters in state 3, so its chance is likewise 17⁄27.

Therefore the highest obtainable probability (17⁄27) is reached by any ball numbered 3 or higher.  The lowest-numbered such ball is 3, so choosing ball 3 maximises your odds.
For any ball the only positions that it can first occupy on the platform are 2 or 3 (except for ball 1,2,3 which start in 1,2,3 respectively).  
Define p1,p2,p3 as the probabilities that a ball eventually gets ejected when it is currently in positions 1,2,3.  Using the rules of the machine and the fact that each piston fires with probability 1⁄3:
•  p1 = 1⁄3 (ejected by piston 1, otherwise it is simply released).  
•  p2 = (1⁄3)·1 + (2⁄3)·p1 = 1⁄3 + (2⁄3)(1⁄3) = 5⁄9.  
•  p3 = (1⁄3)·1 + (1⁄3)·p2 + (1⁄3)·p1 = 1⁄3 + (1⁄3)(5⁄9) + (1⁄3)(1⁄3) = 17⁄27.
Thus a ball that starts in position 3 has the greatest chance of being ejected (17⁄27 ≈ 0.63).
Ball 3 is the only ball guaranteed to begin in position 3, giving it that full 17⁄27 probability.  Every later ball reaches the platform only after one or more firings; each of those balls begins in position 3 with probability 0.6 and in position 2 with probability 0.4, giving an overall ejection chance of 0.6·p3 + 0.4·p2 = 0.6, which is lower than 17⁄27.  Ball 1 (p = 1⁄3) and ball 2 (p = 5⁄9) are even worse.
Therefore the maximum winning probability is achieved by choosing ball 3.

1. Left group: 𒐜 is the sign “eight gesh₂” = 8.

   • Combined value of the right-most (units) position: 50 + 6 = 56.

Total value = 480 + 56 = 536.
The space divides the written value into two base-60 positions.  
• 𒐜 is “eight” (8). This is the left position, so it represents 8 × 60.  
• 𒐐 is “five U” (50) and 𒐚 is “six” (6). Written together without a space they add: 50 + 6 = 56. This is the right (units) position, so it represents 56 × 1.  
Total = 8 × 60 + 56 × 1 = 480 + 56 = 536.
